PATIENT: SYNTHETIC PATIENT 19  MRN 9923000019  DOB 08/02/1978
PROCEDURE: Ion robotic bronchoscopy
INDICATION: 3.0 cm left lower lobe posterior basal PET-avid lesion; prior treated lung cancer. Tissue diagnosis requested.
ANESTHESIA: General anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway
After informed consent and time-out, a therapeutic bronchoscope was introduced under general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway. Airway
inspection to the first subsegmental level showed no obstructing endobronchial lesion. The Ion robotic platform was docked and a deliberate workflow
with fluoroscopy, radial EBUS, and cone-beam confirmation was performed. The target was a 3.0 cm lesion in the left lower lobe posterior basal. Imaging
confirmation used DT. Initial fluoroscopy suggested near-target positioning. Radial probe EBUS demonstrated blunted eccentric radial signal. A
cone-beam or tomographic spin was then obtained to assess tool-to-lesion relationship, after which the catheter was adjusted as needed and repeat
fluoroscopy was performed. Once tool-in-lesion or satisfactory tool-to-lesion relationship was confirmed, lesion sampling proceeded. Samples obtained
included TBNA x5; forceps biopsies x10; brushings x2; BAL x1; cryobiopsies x3. Technical difficulty: No. Limitation(s): None. Associated linear EBUS
staging was then performed. Surveyed stations included 7 (10.1 mm), 4R (7.2 mm), 11R (8.9 mm), 10R (7.4 mm). Sampled stations: 7 x4 (malignant
cells on ROSE); 4R x3 (negative on ROSE); 11R x4 (negative on ROSE). At the end of the case, the airway was reinspected, blood/secretions were
suctioned, and there was no active bleeding.
EBL: <5 mL
COMPLICATIONS: Post-biopsy airway oozing, controlled with dilute epinephrine saline
IMPRESSION: Successful ion robotic bronchoscopy targeting of the left lower lobe posterior basal lesion. Associated EBUS staging was performed. Minor
immediate complication: post-biopsy airway oozing, controlled with dilute epinephrine saline.
PLAN: Recover in PACU; post-procedure chest radiograph per protocol; await final pathology; integrate EBUS staging into treatment planning
